cards.explanation: The answer is False. Peter says, "…do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you." (1 Peter 4:12) He tells them not to treat the trial as something strange. I think that's a gentle way of telling them to steady themselves, friends.

The word is rejoice, friends. Peter says, "But rejoice that you share in the sufferings of Christ…" (1 Peter 4:13) He doesn't say to enjoy the pain. He points them to the One they're sharing it with. Now THAT is a turn I did not see coming.

The reason is that they share in Christ's sufferings, friends. Peter says, "But rejoice that you share in the sufferings of Christ…" (1 Peter 4:13) Their reason isn't about how tough they are. It's about who they're sharing it with. That's a reason worth leaning on.

The answer is True, friends! Peter says, "If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed…" (1 Peter 4:14) An insult doesn't sound like a blessing to me. I've been called a worn-out stamper, and I did NOT feel blessed that day. But Peter says it plainly, and I'll take his word over my feelings.

The reason is that the Spirit of glory rests on them, friends. Peter says they're blessed "…because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you." (1 Peter 4:14) The Spirit is the Holy Spirit, one of the Three I believe in. So the insult is real, but so is the One resting on them.

The word is ashamed, friends. Peter says, "But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name." (1 Peter 4:16) The name Christian is not something to be ashamed of. Peter tells them to glorify God for it instead.

Peter asks what awaits those who disobey the gospel, friends. He says, "and if it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who disobey the gospel of God?" (1 Peter 4:17) He asks it as a question and leaves it hanging. I think that's a heavy one to sit with.

They should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator, friends. Peter says they "…should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good." (1 Peter 4:19) Entrust means putting something in good hands. I once handed my best batch to someone else and held my breath, but this Creator is faithful, and Peter says so.

The answer is False, friends. Peter says those who suffer according to God's will "…should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good." (1 Peter 4:19) They keep on doing good, with no pause button. I've tried pausing a batch once, and the dough had other ideas.
